testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Cargo on a flatbed trailer or trailer without sides must be:

options.text: Loose so it can shift when the vehicle turns.
Heavy enough that it won't shift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strapped down.
questions.explanation: Cargo on a flatbed trailer or trailer without sides must be securely tied down. This keeps it from shifting or falling off while the vehicle moves.

questions.question: To prevent your tires and engine from overheating in hot weather, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your speed.
questions.explanation: Faster driving makes your engine and tires hotter. In very hot weather, slowing down helps prevent overheating.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning light comes on while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Exit the road and park as soon as safely possible.
Stop where you are and park.
Turn on your hazard lights and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the road and park as soon as safely possible.
questions.explanation: When the low pressure warning light comes on, safely exit the road and park your vehicle as soon as you can. Low air pressure means your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: If a tire fails, you should:

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
Check your tires after the vehicle stops completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your tires after the vehicle stops completely.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly if a tire fails. Do not use the brakes. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. When it slows down a lot, brake very gently. Pull off the road and stop. Then check your tires.

questions.question: When carrying cargo, you must check that it is secure:

options.text: Every 150 miles or every three hours of driving.
Only after going up a hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles or every three hours of driving.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles. The driver is responsible for keeping the cargo safely secured the whole trip.

questions.question: When driving, you should:

options.text: Always drive at the posted speed limit.
Always drive slightly below the posted speed limit.
Adjust your speed based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust your speed based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast causes many crashes. You must always adjust your speed to match the road and traffic conditions around you.

questions.question: When checking engine belts during the vehicle inspection test:

options.text: Belts should be checked for tightness, with up to three inches of play allowed.
The water pump belt does not need to be checked.
The air compressor belt should be removed.
You must identify any items that are not belt-driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must identify any items that are not belt-driven.
questions.explanation: Check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts for cracks and frays. Allow up to three-quarters of an inch of play in the center of each belt. If any of these items are not belt-driven, identify them. Make sure their parts work properly, are not damaged or leaking, and are mounted securely.

questions.question: Why should your mirrors show the road behind you and part of your vehicle?

options.text: Seeing only the road might make the driver carsick.
Seeing part of the truck gives you a point of reference.
It is against the law to show only the road.
You need to see reflections of surrounding vehicles on the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seeing part of the truck gives you a point of reference.
questions.explanation: Part of your vehicle should be visible in your mirrors. This helps you judge how close other drivers and objects are to your vehicle.

questions.question: What does intrastate driving mean?

options.text: Traveling from one state to another state

questions.correctAnswerText: Traveling within one state only
questions.explanation: Intrastate driving means you drive your commercial vehicle only within one state. The cargo you carry must not be part of a trip that started or will end outside of that state.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice that forms on road surfaces.
questions.correctAnswerText: Black ice
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road surface through it, so it looks like wet pavement. Be very careful when temperatures are below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, what should you do?

options.text: Choose your own route to show your driving skills.
Follow the directions given by the examiner.
Bring a passenger to sit with you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the examiner.
questions.explanation: You must follow the examiner's directions during the on-road driving test. The examiner will never ask you to drive unsafely.

questions.question: What does poor weight balance do to a vehicle?

options.text: Makes the vehicle harder to handle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes the vehicle harder to handle.
questions.explanation: Poor weight balance makes a vehicle harder and less safe to handle.

questions.question: After driving over a bridge during the skills test, what may the examiner ask you to recall?

options.text: The weight limit posted on the bridge.
The color of a sign you passed.
How many traffic lanes were on the bridge.
Whether there was a crosswalk on the bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The weight limit posted on the bridge.
questions.explanation: The examiner may ask you to remember the weight limit posted on the bridge after you drive over it.

questions.question: How should you press the brake pedal when stopping?
questions.correctAnswerText: Press it down gradually.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down gradually to bring your vehicle to a slow, safe stop.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.correctAnswerText: Axle brake system
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system.

questions.question: What can happen if you use the parking brake in very wet, freezing weather?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and prevent the vehicle from moving.
The brakes may suddenly release by themselves.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and prevent the vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: In very wet, freezing weather, the parking brake can freeze and stop your vehicle from moving.

questions.question: A vehicle stopped at a green light may mean the driver:
questions.correctAnswerText: Is impaired.
questions.explanation: A vehicle stopped at a green light is a sign that the driver may be impaired. Drivers who are intoxicated, drowsy, using drugs, or ill can create danger. One sign of impairment is stopping in wrong places like at green lights.

questions.question: If you stop on a highway, how far behind your vehicle should warning devices be placed?
questions.correctAnswerText: 10, 100, and 200 feet
questions.explanation: Place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet behind your vehicle when stopped on a highway.

questions.question: When checking tires during vehicle inspection, what should you look for?

options.text: More wear on the inside than the outside.
More wear on the outside than the inside.
More wear in the middle than on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even wear across all tires.
questions.explanation: Your tire treads should be worn evenly when you check them during the vehicle inspection.

questions.question: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, what will the ABS do?

options.text: It will still improve your steering control.
It will help others see when you brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will still improve your steering control.
questions.explanation: If only your tractor has ABS, it will still improve your steering control. Watch your trailer and ease up on the brakes if it begins to swing out.

questions.question: When using road speed to decide when to shift gears, you should:

options.text: Learn what speeds work for each gear and shift up when needed.
Watch other vehicles and try to match their speed.
Watch other trucks and shift when they shift.
Use the speed limit as your guide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn what speeds work for each gear and shift up when needed.
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift to a higher gear. The first is engine speed (rpm). Read your vehicle's manual to learn the rpm range and shift up when you reach the top. The second is road speed (mph). Learn which speeds work for each gear. Watch your speedometer and shift up as needed.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located ____ a brake drum.
questions.correctAnswerText: Inside
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are attached to the wheels and located on the axles. The parts that make the vehicle stop are found inside the drum brake.

questions.question: If you drive a vehicle with a manual transmission, you can prevent it from rolling backward when starting from a stop by:

options.text: Partially engaging the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake pedal.
Putting the vehicle in reverse before moving forward.
Fully engaging the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake pedal.
Putting the vehicle in neutral before moving forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partially engaging the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To stop your vehicle from rolling backward when starting, partially engage the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake. Use the parking brake whenever needed to prevent rolling back.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Drive faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have an emergency plan.
questions.explanation: While driving, constantly look ahead to spot hazards early. Plan what you will do if a hazard becomes dangerous.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Help you see a wider area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Many large vehicles use curved convex mirrors. Convex mirrors let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, you should:

options.text: Get special permits and follow special rules.
Honk at other drivers to make them move out of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules.
questions.explanation: Wide, long, or heavy loads may need special permits. Drivers carrying these loads may have restrictions, such as only being allowed to drive at certain times.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must be able to do all of the following about oil, except:

options.text: Show the oil level is in a safe range.
Show the oil level is above the refill mark.
Show the oil level is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show the oil level is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show where the dipstick is, show the oil level is in a safe range, and show the oil level is above the refill mark.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.
Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Do not use tricks like flashing lights to help them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase your distance from the vehicle ahead, avoid sudden moves, and do not use tricks like flashing lights. Speeding up may make it worse by causing them to tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: If you operate a school bus, you are considered to be driving under the influence of alcohol if your blood alcohol content (BAC) is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.02 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: A school bus driver is considered to be driving under the influence if their blood alcohol content is 0.02 percent or higher.

questions.question: Before driving downhill, you should:

options.text: Only use the brakes to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a lower gear.
questions.explanation: On steep downhill slopes, use the engine's braking power as your main way to control speed. Slow down and shift to a lower gear before starting down the hill. Using only brakes can cause them to overheat and become less effective.

questions.question: If you notice a safety or mechanical problem while driving, you should:

options.text: Ignore it and hope it goes away.
Write a report describing the problem.
Avoid using that part and hope no one notices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write a report describing the problem.
questions.explanation: At the end of each driving shift, you may need to write a report about the vehicle. Report any problems that could affect safety or cause mechanical failure.

questions.question: When a construction worker is near the road, you should:

options.text: Wait until construction is finished before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: In construction zones, follow posted speed limits. Slow down even more when workers are near the road.

questions.question: To deal with blind spots, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than other vehicles so they cannot pass you.
Stay in the left lane to only worry about vehicles on your right.
Check your mirrors often and know where other vehicles are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors often and know where other vehicles are.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently. This helps you spot vehicles moving into your blind spots.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: When crossing railroad tracks, do not stop, change gears, pass, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.question: At dawn or dusk, other drivers have trouble seeing you. You can improve visibility by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turning on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dawn or dusk, and in snow or rain, turn on your headlights so other drivers can see your vehicle.

questions.question: Leaking shock absorbers:
questions.correctAnswerText: Indicate a dangerous problem.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds the axles in place. Damaged parts like leaking shock absorbers can be dangerous and must be fixed.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: For a vehicle with power steering, the hoses should be checked for:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leaks.
questions.explanation: Check power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look specifically for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: To test a parking brake, the vehicle should:

options.text: Be in low gear while you try to drive forward.
Be driven while the parking brake is on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be in low gear while you try to drive forward.
questions.explanation: To test the parking brake: fasten your seatbelt, set the parking brake, release the trailer parking brake if needed, put the vehicle in low gear, and try to drive forward. If the parking brake does not hold, it needs to be repaired.

questions.question: When backing up, it is best to:

options.text: Use only the passenger side mirror.
Turn toward the passenger side whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a helper if possible.
questions.explanation: When backing up, go slowly and use both mirrors. Use a helper to watch your blind spots if possible. You and the helper should agree on a stop signal.

questions.question: When should placards be used?

options.text: Any time a vehicle is carrying hazardous materials.
If there is empty space in the truck.
If the hazardous materials in the truck weigh more than 200 pounds.
If the hazardous materials create an inhalation hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time a vehicle is carrying hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on the outside of vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They show what type of materials are being carried and warn others of the hazards.

questions.question: A driver will lose their CDL for a minimum of ____ for a first conviction of driving a commercial vehicle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of 0.04 percent.
questions.correctAnswerText: One year
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive a commercial vehicle if your BAC is 0.04 percent or higher. You will lose your license for at least one year for a first conviction of driving a commercial vehicle under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

questions.question: Joggers who wear headsets:

options.text: Are usually aware of their surroundings.
May not be aware of their surroundings.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be aware of their surroundings.
questions.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear traffic sounds and may not know you are there.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce cell phone distractions while driving?

options.text: Stay on a single call for the entire trip.
Turn the phone off before driving.
Only use the phone to accept incoming calls.
Use the phone to text instead of talk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the phone off before driving.
questions.explanation: Avoid cell phone distractions by turning off your phone before you start driving. Keep it off until you reach your destination.

questions.question: If a truck's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working, what happens?

options.text: The truck will have no brakes.
The truck should only be driven at slow speeds.
The truck will still have brakes.
The truck will have no brakes on its left side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: If the ABS fails, the vehicle will still have normal brakes. Drive and brake as you normally would.

questions.question: When alley docking, where should your vehicle be parked?

options.text: With the front bumper on the front boundary line.
With the rear wheels over the rear boundary line.
Straight within the boundaries of the parking space.
At an angle within the boundaries of the parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straight within the boundaries of the parking space.
questions.explanation: For alley docking, first pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking area. Your vehicle should be parked straight and stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver involved in a crash ahead of you, what should you do?

options.text: Block the driver in with your vehicle.
Stop at a safe distance and tell police about the aggressive driving you saw.
Keep driving and don't get involved.
Pull over and yell at the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a safe distance and tell police about the aggressive driving you saw.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving an aggressive driver, stop a safe distance away from the scene. Wait for police and tell them about the aggressive behavior you witnessed.

questions.question: When checking the exhaust system, it should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Check the exhaust system to make sure no parts are loose, broken, or missing.

questions.question: When using a helper to back your vehicle, where should they stand?

options.text: In front of the passenger side
In front of the driver side
On the side of the truck
Near the back of the truck

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the back of the truck
questions.explanation: Your helper should stand near the back of the vehicle where you can see them. Before backing, agree on hand signals that you both understand, including a signal to stop.

questions.question: What color is the low air pressure warning light?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes have a low air pressure warning light. It is usually red and may have a buzzer sound with it.
